skill.name: security-quick-review
skill.description: Quick security pass over a change or module covering secrets, injection, auth and access checks, unsafe deserialization, dependency and config risks, with evidence. Use before merging code that handles input, auth, files or money.
skill.summary: Review code changes for likely security issues with scoped evidence, realistic severity, and concrete fixes.
skill.author: agentkitco

security_audit.summary: All five static findings are false positives from Markdown formatting, defensive terminology, and scoped code inspection. The only suggested commands inspect Git changes and history; the skill forbids live exploitation and repeating secret values. No evidence found of malicious instructions, credential exfiltration, or unsafe execution directives.

finding_verdicts.reason: Backticks format git diff and git log -p as inline Markdown, not Ruby or shell substitution. These commands support scoped repository inspection, and the text prohibits repeating secret values.
The inline eval/exec references name unsafe operations to detect during review. They are not executable statements or instructions to invoke either operation.
Lines 31 through 39 contain a fenced Markdown report template with severity labels and placeholders. The fence does not contain executable commands or command substitution.
Private keys appear only as a category of exposed secrets to detect in scoped code and history. The instruction explicitly prohibits repeating secret values, and no actual key material appears.
Line 16 defines review scope and asks for inspection of related called code. It does not request host enumeration, system probing, or unrelated data collection.

content.user_title: Review Code Changes for Security Risks
content.value_statement: Code changes can introduce security problems that routine reviews miss. This skill guides focused AI triage with evidence, realistic severity, and concrete fixes.
actual_capabilities: Defines reviewed and excluded scope, including related code called by a change.
Checks scoped code, Git changes, and history for exposed secrets without repeating secret values.
Reviews untrusted input, injection paths, authentication, authorization, and data exposure.
Examines unsafe operations, dependency changes, configuration risks, and failure behavior.
Structures findings by severity with file locations, abuse explanations, and specific fixes.
Records clean checklist categories, verification gaps, and automated triage limitations.
limitations: Provides AI triage, not a security audit, penetration test, or guarantee that code is secure.
Cannot establish runtime or infrastructure behavior from code alone; unverifiable details must be reported.
Requires accessible source context and tools; it includes no dedicated scanner or test suite.
Does not permit live exploitation and calls for human review of money, health, or identity workflows.

use_cases.title: Check a Pull Request Before Merge
use_cases.description: Review changed input handlers and related code for injection, exposed secrets, and unsafe error behavior.

use_cases.title: Review Access Controls
use_cases.description: Examine routes and actions for missing server-side checks and access to another user's records.

use_cases.title: Inspect Dependency and Configuration Changes
use_cases.description: Review package additions, lockfiles, debug settings, and new CI or cloud permissions within the selected change.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Small Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current diff for likely security issues. State the scope, cite evidence, suggest fixes, and list anything you cannot verify.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: focused review before merging a small change.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect an Endpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [endpoint] and its called code for untrusted input, injection, authentication, authorization, and data exposure. Report evidence and concrete fixes without live exploitation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: inspect a specific application entry point.

prompt_templates.title: Check Secrets and Configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [directory] and its scoped Git changes and history for exposed secrets, dependency risks, and configuration weaknesses. Never reproduce secret values; recommend rotation when needed.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: evaluate sensitive configuration or dependency changes.

prompt_templates.title: Trace a Sensitive Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [workflow] across changed code and called modules. Trace authorization, input boundaries, unsafe operations, and failure behavior. Separate evidence from uncertainty and identify human-review needs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: trace a sensitive workflow across modules.

output_examples.input: Illustrative scenario: an endpoint accepts a record identifier but never verifies that the caller owns the record.
output: Scope: the changed endpoint and its authorization checks; deployment behavior was not reviewed.
HIGH: Missing ownership validation could let an authenticated caller access another user's record by changing the identifier.
Fix: enforce record-level authorization on the server before returning data.
A real finding must include the affected file and line; this illustration has no source attachment.
Limits: automated triage, not a security audit.

output_examples.input: Illustrative scenario: a credential was removed from the current change but remains visible in repository history.
output: Scope: the selected change and its repository history.
HIGH: A historical credential remains exposed even after removal from current code.
Fix: rotate or revoke the credential and investigate its use; deleting current text does not invalidate it.
Evidence should identify the source location without reproducing the secret value.
Could not verify: whether the credential remains active.

best_practices: Specify the diff, directory, endpoint, or workflow and include relevant called code.
Require file and line evidence, realistic impact, concrete fixes, and explicit verification gaps.
Rotate exposed secrets and obtain human review for workflows handling money, health, or identity data.
anti_patterns: Treating a clean triage report as proof that an application is secure.
Pasting secret values into reports or assuming deletion removes historical exposure.
Attempting live exploitation or accepting generic vulnerability lists without source evidence.

faq.question: Is this a complete security audit?
faq.answer: No. It provides focused AI triage, not a security audit or penetration test.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The marketplace lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Review depth depends on available source context and tool access.

faq.question: What does the review cover?
faq.answer: It covers secrets, untrusted input, injection, access controls, data exposure, unsafe operations, dependencies, configuration, and failure behavior.

faq.question: Does it run attacks against live systems?
faq.answer: No. The skill prohibits live exploitation and allows code inspection and local tests.

faq.question: How does it handle exposed secrets?
faq.answer: It requests source locations without secret values and recommends rotation because removal from current code does not erase Git history.

faq.question: What should a useful report include?
faq.answer: Include scope, severity, source evidence, an abuse explanation, concrete fixes, clean categories, verification gaps, and the limits of automated triage.
